name: Hamstring strain recovery
goal: Recover from a pulled hamstring: gentle loading early, then strength in the lengthened position (where re-injuries happen), then a gradual return to running and sprinting.
whoFor: People with a mild to moderate hamstring strain (a sudden pull or twinge in the back of the thigh while running or stretching).
notFor: A large bruise high near the buttock with a pop and difficulty walking (possible tendon tear): see a doctor quickly
trackedMetric: Pain in the back of the thigh when walking fast or bending (0-10)
painRules: Exercises should feel like work, not pain: stay at 2-3 out of 10 or less. Stretch only gently, and only once it doesn't hurt.
redFlags: A pop with a large bruise high in the back of the thigh, a gap you can feel, or difficulty walking
Numbness or tingling down the leg
Calf swelling with warmth (possible blood clot)
Pain that keeps getting worse after the first few days

phases.name: Early loading
phases.entryCriteria: Recent strain, sore to walk fast or bend.
phases.exitCriteria: Brisk walking and the bridge hold are pain-free.

phases.name: Strength in length
phases.exitCriteria: Single-leg deadlifts and bridges without pain, and a full pain-free stretch.

phases.name: Return to running and sprinting
phases.exitCriteria: Full-speed running feels normal. Keep Nordics once or twice a week to prevent re-injury.

items.note: Build from 60% to near full speed over the weeks.

references: Askling CM, et al. 2013. Acute hamstring injuries in Swedish elite football: a prospective randomised controlled clinical trial comparing two rehabilitation protocols. Br J Sports Med 47:953-9.
Petersen J, et al. 2011. Preventive effect of eccentric training on acute hamstring injuries in men's soccer: a cluster-randomized controlled trial. Am J Sports Med 39:2296-303.
